name: CH-47 Chinook
summary: Tandem-rotor heavy-lift helicopter used by the Army for troops, artillery and cargo, with special-operations MH-47Gs and a small number of civil logging/firefighting examples.

wings: Two large three-blade rotors in tandem, front and rear, turning in opposite directions
Rear rotor mounted on a tall aft pylon, higher than the front rotor
engines: Two engines in external pods on either side of the rear rotor pylon
Exhausts pointing straight aft from the engine pods
fuselage: Long, boxy, rectangular fuselage with rows of round-cornered windows
Long fuel pods (sponsons) running along the lower sides
Four fixed wheels, two forward and two aft
Rear loading ramp under the aft pylon; MH-47G adds a long refueling probe and nose radar
tail: No conventional fin or stabilizer; the aft pylon forms the tail

tellTales: Two big rotors, one at each end of the fuselage
No tail rotor and no tail fin
Engines hung on the outside of the tall rear pylon

confusedWith.howToTell: The Chinook's two rotors are at the front and back of the fuselage; the Osprey's two rotors sit on wingtip nacelles side by side.
The CH-53E has one huge seven-blade main rotor and a tail rotor; the Chinook has two three-blade rotors and no tail rotor.

usCount.source: US Army CH-47F + MH-47G (FlightGlobal World Air Forces 2025) + ~35 FAA-registered civil CH-47D/234
